title.narrative: e-transformation of policing processes related to contravention UNDP 2022-2027
e-transformation of policing processes related to contravention UNDP 2022-2027

description.narrative: Bidraget kommer att genomföras av UNDP Moldavien och kommer att ha en teknisk karaktär: skapandet av en ny mjukvara för att säkerställa att brotten i Moldavien registreras på digitala sätt, vilket minskar mänsklig faktor och korruption; och att se till att utredningen av brott görs i rätt tid och med fullt ansvar av polisen.

The contribution will be implemented by UNDP Moldova and will have a technical character: the creation of a new soft to ensure the offences in Moldova are registered using digital ways therefore diminishing human factor and corruption; and ensuring the investigation of offences is done in due time and with full accountability by the police.

The new e-contravention case management system, developed through this intervention (conceptualisation, development, piloting, stabilization and roll-out and maintenance), will support the optimization of policing activities in contravention procedure, will improve discipline and institutional control over the contravention cases, will enhance the quality of data produced during the documentation of contraventions, will facilitate the exchange of data between MoI and other justice chain institutions with responsibilities in contravention cases (e.g. prosecution, courts). Furthermore, the new e-contravention case management system will harmonize and enhance collaboration among the 44 state institutions/agents with a mandate to detect and investigate contraventions.Considering the applicable legal provisions and procedures, the e-contravention case management system will ensure the interoperability with case management systems of prosecution and judiciary through the M-Connect e-service. Taken together, these results can increase public confidence in and support for law enforcement and justice processes, enhancing system performance and, ultimately, the integrity of the law.

Results achieved under each project output:
Output 1: Enhanced capabilities to accelerate e-transformation of policing processes related to contravention cases •Working Group involving representatives of relevant MIAs subdivisions established. •Business review of the existing workflows related to contravention cases management within MIA system carried out. •The Concept and Functioning Regulation of the ECCM system drafted and coordinated with the beneficiary. •Technical Specifications for the Development of ECCM system drafted and preliminary validated by the beneficiary. •Technical Specifications for the Development of ECCM system endorsed by the E-Governance Agency (EGA). •Tender documentation for the selection of ECCM system developer drafted and expected to be launched by the end of December 2023 early January 2024. •Review of the regulatory framework related to future ECCM system initiated.
With regards to the Output 2 (Project Management), the achievements are: •Planning and Reporting activities carried out. •Logistic accommodation of the project team carried out. •Legal Expert contracted. •Competition for the selection of one Project IT Expert completed. •Competition for the selection of one Project Associate ongoing.
Activities to be implemented during January-December 2024, with a total budget of USD 503,199 (51% of the total Project budget): •Following an open competition, to contract a specialized company to develop the ECCM system. •Development of the ECCM system to be completed at a level of at least 70%. •Regulatory framework to ensure proper legal grounds for the usage of ECCM system reviewed. •Inter-agency dialogue platform on the ECCM system established. •Awareness activities to support strategic planning and costing for ECCM systems implementation launched. •A Project Associate to be selected and contracted. •Communication Plan, Delivery and Annual Procurement Plan developed. •Financial and logistic management of the project carried out.
Update:
Progress and Achievements (October 2022 December 2023)
During the reporting period, the project focused on laying the foundation for digital transformation. The key achievements include:
- Comprehensive Business Analysis and Stakeholder Consultations
Conducted an in-depth review of workflows related to contravention case management. Consulted police officers, senior management, and digitalization institutions to align expectations. Established a Technical Working Group within MIA to oversee the projects implementation.
- Development of the Terms of Reference for the E-Contraventions System
A detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) was created to guide system development. The ToR was reviewed and endorsed by MIA and the E-Governance Agency. The system will be built using open-source technologies to ensure flexibility for future upgrades.
- Key Features of the Proposed E-Contraventions System
Digitization of contravention case files to improve record-keeping and accessibility. Interoperability with national databases, ensuring real-time access to critical data. Integration of georeferenced evidence, allowing officers to upload location-based proof. Seamless communication with emergency services (112) and judicial case management systems. Mobile and desktop accessibility, enabling officers to work remotely. Advanced reporting and analytics tools to monitor case trends in real-time.
Challenges and Implementation Barriers
While the project has made progress, several challenges and obstacles have slowed implementation:
- Poor Communication with the Beneficiary (MIA) Inconsistent engagement and response times from the Ministry of Internal Affairs (MIA) have caused delays in decision-making and project approvals. Lack of clear coordination channels between UNDP and MIA has sometimes led to misunderstandings and misalignment of priorities. The Technical Working Group, though established, has faced difficulties in obtaining timely feedback and approvals from key MIA stakeholders.
- Delays in Implementation and Decision-Making Approval processes have taken longer than expected, particularly in finalizing the Terms of Reference and securing necessary authorizations. Delays in stakeholder consultations slowed down the finalization of the software specifications. Procurement and tendering risks have also contributed to setbacks, as the complexity of the system requires a highly specialized IT contractor, which has proven challenging to identify.
- Infrastructure and Budgetary Constraints Moldovas existing cloud infrastructure is insufficient to support the full-scale deployment of the new system, requiring additional funding for expansion. The risk that financial offers from developers may exceed the allocated budget remains a concern, potentially requiring adjustments to project scope or securing additional funds. Future maintenance and sustainability beyond 2027 need to be properly planned, as MIA may struggle to cover operational costs once UNDP support ends.
- Regulatory and Institutional Barriers The legal framework for digital policing is still evolving, and regulatory updates are needed to ensure the e-Contraventions system aligns with national laws. Inter-agency coordination issues have created difficulties in ensuring seamless data-sharing between MIA, judiciary, and other law enforcement agencies.
Update 2024: During 2024, the implementation of the project faced significant challenges, particularly with regard to the procurement and contracting process for the e-Contraventions software solution. While efforts were made to advance the development of the system a key deliverable the competitive selection process ultimately failed. This failure stemmed from the disqualification of the top-ranked bidder after all parties had initially approved the vendor, due to late-stage identification of technical inconsistencies with the Terms of Reference during the contract finalization stage. This decision, made in adherence to UNDP procurement policies, unfortunately led to increased tension and a breakdown of trust between UNDP Moldova and the Ministry of Internal Affairs (MOIA).
As a result, cooperation between the implementing and beneficiary institutions has become ineffective, compromising the ability to jointly identify a path forward. Discussions convened in December 2024 explored several potential alternatives including awarding the contract to the second-ranked bidder (which would require significant additional funding), revising technical specifications, or reissuing the tender (which would cause further delays). None of these paths received consensus from key stakeholders.
Following two rounds of reconciliation meetings convened by the Swedish Embassy and mediated between UNDP and MOIA, the parties have identified a mutually acceptable solution and agreed on a revised approach to enable the continuation of the project. The following next steps have been endorsed by all stakeholders:
- Application of HACT Mechanism: UNDP will implement a Harmonized Approach to Cash Transfers (HACT) modality, which involves transferring funds directly to MOIA to implement system-related activities. This is similar to the approach applied under the SSM project.
- Institutional Capacity Assessment: As per HACT requirements, UNDP will contract an independent audit firm to evaluate MOIAs capacity in financial management, procurement, and human resources. This process is expected to take 23 months. Coordination with the audit firm used by Sida under the SSM project will be ensured to streamline efforts.
- Revision of ToR: During the assessment period, MOIA will revise the technical specifications for the e-Contraventions system to fit within the available development budget.
- Project Amendment: The new implementation approach will require a formal amendment to the Contribution Agreement, covering: Adjustment of the Project Document; Extension of the implementation period to include 12 months of system maintenance post-development; A budget top-up
At this stage, Sida has indicated that the proposed solution represents a viable and constructive alternative to termination, given that both UNDP and MOIA have expressed readiness to cooperate and move forward as partners. The agreed approach provides an opportunity to salvage the intended project results while aligning implementation with realistic time frames and institutional capacities.
While the primary outcome launching the development of the e-Contraventions case management system was not achieved, the project still made substantive progress in terms of capacity building, process alignment, and strategic recalibration, all of which are essential to enabling sustainable digital transformation in Moldova's policing sector.
